title: Reduce alert noise & automate on-call runbook for multi-region failover and load-shed scenarios
creator: Asha Kapoor
project: Reliability: Multi-region SLO and Incident Automation
description: This ticket consolidates alerting thresholds, reduces paging noise, and implements an automated on-call runbook for multi-region failover, circuit-breaker activation, and load-shedding events. Goal is to avoid unnecessary pages for transient latency blips while ensuring fast human response for SLO-impacting incidents and automated safe-fail behavior when capacity is exhausted.
acceptance_criteria: Alert volume reduced by >= 60% for the top 10 recurring noisy alerts during normal traffic
PagerDuty pages only for SLO-breaching conditions or successful automated escalation failures
Runbook automated playbooks run end-to-end in staging and trigger correct circuit-breaker and routing changes
Post-incident dashboard shows correct root-cause tags and automatic incident notes in Confluence link
Rollback path documented and tested: revert changes and restore pre-runbook alerting within 15 minutes
runbook_steps: 1) Triage summary: identify affected region(s), service (runtime/gateway/kv-cache), SLI delta, and recent deploys.
2) Check dashboards: SLO heatmap (red threshold), per-region P95/P99, queue length, GPU utilization, EB-queue metrics.
3) Determine if automated mitigation has fired: circuit-breaker active? load-shed policy applied? prefix cached?
4) If circuit-breaker is open: validate reason (backpressure vs dependency failure) and escalate to runtime on-call unless automated fallback succeeded.
5) Multi-region failover: if region A latency > SLO for 5m and region B healthy, trigger routing switch using safe-rollout script (scripts/routing/safe_failover.sh).
6) Run load-shed reversal: confirm CPU/GPU recover to <70% and queue drain <200 before lifting shed policy. Use control-plane API call: POST /admin/load-shed/lift.
7) Pager flow: Incident start → primary on-call for 5m → if unresolved escalate to secondary and send automated diagnostic bundle (logs + traces + KV cache snapshot) to #infra-incident Slack channel.
8) Post-mortem stub: create incident page from template, attach automation run logs and PRs for remediation within 48h.
9) Rollback: restore pre-failover routing and disable emergency scaling if system stable for 10m; document timestamps and operator name.
10) Close incident only after verifying SLOs recovered and stakeholders acknowledged.
alert_rules_changes: Reduce sensitivity of runtime-p99-alert: change from 3 datapoints > threshold in 1m to 3 datapoints > threshold in 5m (reduces transient noise).
Add circuit-breaker-alert channel: only page when cb.open_duration > 1m AND (error-rate > 1% OR queue_length > 1000).
Introduce 'SLO-impacting' tag for alerts that map to customer-visible SLOs. Only SLO-impacting alerts will page immediately; others route to #alerts for 30m aggregation.
Implement suppression window for deploy-related errors: suppress known-deploy-error alerts for 10m after a verified deployment event from CI metadata.
Create heartbeat monitors for cross-region failover automation to detect misfires and generate a high-priority page if automation fails to complete in 3 minutes.
automation_playbooks: Failover orchestrator (playbook): checks region health, updates routing weight in small increments, verifies successful warm-up of model workers, and rebalances traffic. Runs with dry-run and canary gates.
Load-shed policy engine: applies shedding rules based on queue-depth and GPU contention; includes slow-backoff and per-customer grace thresholds.
Circuit-breaker auto-close policy: attempts gradual reconnection after exponential backoff and validates success with a canary stream for 2 minutes before full close.
Incident triage bot: collects diagnostics, annotates PagerDuty incident, posts a summary to Slack #infra-incident, and creates a Confluence incident page pre-filled with runbook checklist.
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting with reliability, runtime, and platform routing teams. Defined scope and success metrics.
2026-03-03: Drafted initial alert sensitivity changes; runtime team agreed to p99 hysteresis change. PR created: github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/4292.
2026-03-05: Implemented suppression for deploy-related alerts in Alertmanager staging. Observing ~40% reduction in noisy pages during canary deploys.
2026-03-08: Built and deployed incident triage bot prototype to staging. Bot posts diagnostics to #infra-incident. PR: github.com/redwood/tools/pulls/318.
2026-03-10: Ran staged automation test: simulated region A outage, orchestrator moved 15% traffic per step and completed failover in 4m; identified race condition in KV cache warm-up.
2026-03-12: Fixed KV cache warm-up race (runtime patch: github.com/redwood/runtime/commit/2a9c5ef). Updated runbook to wait for cache-ready event.
review_feedback: PM (Dana Ortiz): please add explicit business-owner notify step for customer-impacting incidents.
Design (Jules Moreno): ensure runbook copywriting is readable on mobile for on-call engineers.
Security (Ravi Singh): confirm the triage bot does not leak credentials in diagnostics bundle. Added filter in staging.
SRE Lead (Katarina Novak): prefer 5m sustained SLO breach before paging to reduce noise from transient spikes.
next_steps: 1) Roll the new alerting rules to production for a limited subset of services (gateway + runtime) and monitor page volume for 72h.
2) Complete automated orchestration smoke-tests across three regions and validate canary gating behavior.
3) Add business-owner notification step and finalize mobile-friendly runbook text.
4) Schedule a tabletop drill with on-call rotation to exercise the automation and escalation path (target week 2026-03-23).
5) Post-mortem after drill and adjust thresholds based on observed operator behavior.
